utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-97-24-A, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Registrar. Could I now have the appearances for the parties. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Katharina Margetts for the Prosecution, together with counsel, Michelle Jarvis, and our case manager, Mr. Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Margetts. The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Stakic, can you hear me and understand the proceedings in your language? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can hear and understand in my language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic, you may be seated. THE APPELLANT: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This a Status Conference held in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation to thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. On 6th October 2005 at the end of hearing of the appeals in this case, the Bench asked the parties whether they had any issues to raise. Almost 120 days have now passed since the hearing of the appeals. Mr. Stakic, do you have any issues to raise in relation to your detention? Do you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any new problems, thank God. I have the standard problems with my blood pressure, and I'm taking medicines for that. And I agreed with the doctor to make some more tests and perhaps to go and see the cardiologist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stakic, you may be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The parties' submissions on their respective appeals from the trial judgement have now been complete for some time. As you know, the Appeals Chamber conducted a hearing on the Prosecution and Defence appeals in -- last October, 4, 5 -- on the 4th, 5th, and the 6th. I would like to thank both the Prosecution and the Defence for having helped to make that hearing run smoothly. The Appeals Chamber is now preparing a judgement in this case. Both the Prosecution and the Defence, I am told, have indicated to court staff that they are anxious to know when the Appeals Chamber will be issuing the judgement. Unfortunately, I cannot yet answer that question. I can tell them that we are working hard on the judgement and that I certainly would promise that when we are ready to issue the judgement the parties would be notified as soon as possible. Before concluding this Status Conference, I want to ask counsel for the Prosecution and the Defence whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Ms. Margetts?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no issues from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is nothing new on our side either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close. The court will now rise.
